post_text:
Stop treating Redis like a temporary scratchpad for your database.

You are killing your performance with unnecessary synchronization logic. Redis is a primary database, not just a cache. Most engineers get this wrong by treating it as an optional sidecar. They build fragile cache-aside patterns that invite race conditions and data inconsistency. In reality, Redis’s native data structures are robust enough to be your source of truth for high-throughput state. I once moved a massive session management system entirely out of Postgres and into Redis. We deleted 500 lines of synchronization boilerplate and slashed P99 latency by 120ms. Persistence is a solved problem; stop being terrified of AOF and RDB snapshots. If your entire system collapses the moment Redis goes down, it was never just a cache to begin with. Stop lying to yourself and treat it like the database it actually is. ⚡
lesson_extracted: Treating Redis as a secondary cache instead of a primary data store creates unnecessary complexity and architectural fragility.
